items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: I was playing with him at the time... We were playing together.

ctx.x: He's even thinking of starting to play the string bass. Yeah.

George Foster. You know him, don't you? Bass player. And he had a brother named, uh, Willie. Charlie! Willie, yeah. Willie, yeah. Willie, yeah. Willie, yeah. Willie, yeah. Willie, yeah. Willie, yeah. Willie, yeah. Willie, yeah. White fella. Yeah, yeah. I know him. Because he'd play violin, and he'd get up a violin once there and get a ten of banjo. He was the best runner on a ten of banjo. But he didn't play so long, you know. He was in Baton Rouge, you see. He was in the Blaster and Bricklay, you know. He was…
Ask him who were some of the bands in Baton Rouge.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: So we'd give it to Bob Lyons. And Bob Lyons sent them 75 dollars deposit.

ctx.x: Where did you work with Wesley Dones?

So where did you work with Wesley Dones? Well, we worked all around the city, until we'd give a dance ourselves with the rest of Baton Rouge. And then we got to play the concert. And after that, the right thing we got traded by the old band. And when they got ready to hire, we had so many dates we couldn't make it. So we'd give it to Bob Lyons. And Bob Lyons sent them 75 dollars deposit. And somehow, they wrote back to us and told him they didn't care for him so much he could keep the money, you know. So they…
Ask him who he would use on second cornet.
